verdicts.reason: TestProcessDetectors.setUp's entire body is `super().setUp()`, which is exactly what Python would do without the override; it is dead code left behind when StatefulDetectorHandlerTestMixin's setUp was folded into BaseDetectorHandlerTest.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler previously implemented evaluate() and was instantiable; after reparenting to StatefulDetectorHandler it is `pass` with four inherited abstractmethods unimplemented, so the question about intent points at a genuine regression rather than a neutral placeholder.
The docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`" while the signature on line 226-228 now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult].

BaseDetectorHandlerTest.build_handler takes detector_type, but every one of the ten calls in subclasses (lines 329, 338, 350, 381, 425, 442, 487, 507, 534, 582) is a bare self.build_handler(); the calls at 285-298 belong to TestKeyBuilders' own build_handler.

counter_names = ["test1", "test2"] is a mutable class attribute with no ClassVar annotation (the RUF012 pattern), though the base declares counter_names as an abstract property, so a literal ClassVar annotation may itself trip mypy's class-vs-instance override check; the observation stands, the proposed fix is arguable.

create_detector_and_conditions(self, type: str | None = None) shadows the builtin inside the function body; the same collision is what forced the `import builtins` workaround in models/detector.py, so the naming hazard is demonstrably live in this codebase.

IssueOccurrence defines an explicit __eq__ returning self.id == other.id, and build_mock_occurrence_and_event hardcodes id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578", so every occurrence the helper builds compares equal regardless of fingerprint, priority or group_key.

In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe the expected occurrence is built with group_key "val1" and value 6 while evaluate_group_key_value is called with "group_key" and 10; the assertion still passes only because IssueOccurrence.__eq__ ignores fingerprint, so the new hook's inputs go unvalidated.

The duplicate-group-key branch and its logger.error were deleted along with test_state_results_multi_group_dupe, and nothing in the new dict-returning evaluate() docstring or DetectorHandler contract states that keys must be unique and match result.group_key — evaluate() silently keys on result.group_key, so a mismatched handler now overwrites instead of logging.
The packet sets group_2 to 10 but build_mock_occurrence_and_event is called with value=6; it passes because the helper never references its `value` parameter, so the argument mismatch is invisible.

process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result (which produces to Kafka) for every result before handler.commit_state_updates(); if the commit raises, neither the dedupe value nor DetectorState is persisted, so the next packet re-evaluates the same transition and produces the occurrence again — previously that could only re-emit a StatusChangeMessage.

`import builtins` and the `builtins.type[GroupType] | None` return annotation carry no comment, and the reason given is correct: Detector declares `type = models.CharField(...)` at line 42, which shadows the builtin for annotations resolved in class scope.
Same mismatch as stated: data packet has {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10} while the group_2 expected occurrence is built with value=6.

StatefulDetectorHandler declares exactly those four abstractmethods (counter_names property, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) and derives from abc.ABC, so MetricAlertDetectorHandler with only `pass` is not instantiable; Detector.detector_handler instantiates it via group_type.detector_handler(self), meaning any metric_alert_fire detector would raise TypeError. It is latent today only because nothing calls process_detectors in production yet.
`value` appears in the signature but is referenced nowhere in the body — only handler, group_key and new_status are used — which is precisely why the wrong-value call sites go undetected.

Every element of the chain checks out: __eq__/__hash__ are overridden to use id alone, the helper hardcodes one id, and @freeze_time(tick=False) makes the event_data timestamps identical too — so the PR's new occurrence assertions constrain nothing, as the value and group-key mismatches that still pass demonstrate.

project_id is still the XXX-marked property returning 1, and it now flows into the IssueOccurrence path that reaches produce_occurrence_to_kafka; the only thing currently preventing writes against project 1 is that process_detectors has no production caller (grep finds only the __init__ re-export), which is not a mechanism anyone declared.

Confirms the same call: in test_state_results_multi_group the second occurrence uses value=6 against a packet value of 10, so nothing in the suite pins how `value` reaches build_occurrence_and_event_data.

mock.assert_has_calls only requires the listed calls to be present and never bounds the total, so an extra produce_occurrence_to_kafka would pass — weaker than the assert_called_once_with used in test_state_results, and this is the test that replaced the deleted duplicate-group-key test.

The comment "TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" sits directly above the line that now reads `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[...])` — the abstraction exists and is in use, so the TODO is stale.

The wrong group key is real — 'val1' yields fingerprint [f"{id}:val1"] while evaluate_group_key_value builds [f"{id}:group_key"] — but the stated consequence is wrong: the assertion does not break, because IssueOccurrence.__eq__ compares id only and both ids are the hardcoded constant.
